articles.title: First-of-its-kind registration initiative for PM Modi’s Vadodara event; seats fill within an hour
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: All seats for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s programme in Vadodara were booked within an hour after public registration opened on BookMySho.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: All seats for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s programme in Vadodara were booked within an hour after public registration opened on BookMyShow, in what the government described as a first-of-its-kind initiative.The Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) used the private digital platform to manage free registrations for the programme scheduled for Tuesday. Once all seats were booked, registration was closed, while more than 42,000 additional applicants were placed on a waiting list.The registration system will also be used for digital entry at the venue. Registered participants will receive a digital M-Ticket through their BookMyShow account, carrying a secure live QR code for entry verification.The registration, verification, venue entry and seating process is being managed digitally, according to the press release. The system is intended to facilitate entry and manage movement of people at the venue.PM Modi to inaugurate and dedicate projects in VadodaraPM Modi will visit Vadodara on Tuesday, where he will inaugurate, dedicate and lay the foundation stones for several development projects.Among the projects he will dedicate to the nation are three sections of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC), covering 326 route kilometres and developed at a cost of more than Rs 20,700 crore.The sections are Sanand (North)-Makarpura, New Umbergaon-New Saphale and New Saphale-JNPT. Their commissioning will provide direct connectivity to Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority and, according to the official statement, facilitate movement of EXIM cargo and connectivity between industrial centres and ports.PM Modi will also flag off freight train services from New Sanand (North), New Makarpura, New Umbergaon and New JNPT in Mumbai.A new train service between Vadodara and Tanda Road will also be flagged off, benefiting passengers in Vadodara, Chhota Udepur and Alirajpur districts.Railway, highway projects also on agendaThe Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone for three railway projects spanning 329 km and costing more than Rs 9,700 crore.These include the Vadodara-Ratlam third and fourth railway lines, the Miyagam Karjan-Choranda-Malsar gauge conversion project and the Vishwamitri-Dabhoi doubling project.He will also lay the foundation stone for three national highway projects costing around Rs 1,780 crore, along with various Gujarat government projects worth around Rs 2,600 crore.After the Vadodara programme, PM Modi will travel to Mumbai to inaugurate the Global Fintech Fest 2026.The seventh edition of the conference will be held from September 8 to 11. Its theme this year is “Potential to Impact: Agentic AI, Tokenisation, Quantum - Trusted, Connected, Global Systems for Inclusive Finance.”The conference brings together policymakers, regulators, central banks, financial institutions, fintech companies, technology firms, investors and academia to discuss developments in the future of finance.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Porn to pay for drones? How Ukraine plans to turn adult content into a war revenue stream
articles.summary: International News: Ukraine is considering legalising and taxing its adult entertainment industry as the government looks for additional revenue to support the country's .
articles.body: Ukraine is considering legalising and taxing its adult entertainment industry as the government looks for additional revenue to support the country's war effort against Russia, The Wall Street Journal reported.Pornography is currently illegal in Ukraine, with the production, possession or distribution of pornographic material punishable by up to seven years in prison.Despite the ban, the country's adult content industry has grown significantly and operates in a legal grey area, with allegations of corruption involving law enforcement.Ukrainian authorities have also begun seeking taxes from adult content creators. But those who declare their earnings can potentially expose themselves to prosecution under the country's pornography laws.Ukrainian MP pushes for legalisationUkrainian lawmaker Yaroslav Zhelezniak is backing legislation that would legalise pornography and bring the industry into the formal economy.He estimates that the move could generate up to $25 million in tax revenue annually, enough to help fund the purchase of up to 30,000 drones for Ukraine’s war effort."These women either don’t pay taxes and face criminal charges for that, or they pay taxes and get charged with violating pornography laws,” Zhelezniak, who chairs the finance committee in Ukraine’s Parliament, told the WSJ.“It’s a tragicomic situation,” he added.Supporters of the proposal say legalisation could generate additional tax revenue, reduce corruption and ease the burden on law enforcement at a time when Ukraine is fighting a prolonged war.The scale of Ukraine's online adult entertainment industry has grown sharply in recent years. According to data cited by the WSJ, Fenix International, the parent company of OnlyFans, found that about 7,900 Ukrainians earned more than $131 million through the platform in 2023.However, creators who disclosed their earnings to tax authorities have faced the risk of being investigated for allegedly producing illegal adult content.One of them, Svitlana Dvornikova, told the newspaper that police seized $20,000 in cash, her laptop and hard drives during a search of her home. Several Ukrainian OnlyFans creators, including Dvornikova, have since left the country or temporarily moved elsewhere in Europe.Petition gains supportTax lawyer Lesia Mykhalenko, who has represented more than 100 OnlyFans models, said the current system places an unnecessary burden on both creators and the legal system.“This is a victimless crime,” Mykhalenko told the WSJ. “It unnecessarily burdens the legal system at a time when we should be focused on defending the country.”After a case was filed against her, Dvornikova submitted a petition on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's website. She described herself as a "conscientious taxpayer" and argued that the government should not treat her as a criminal.She said she had paid nearly $900,000 in taxes, which she claimed was equivalent to “hundreds of Russians killed on the front line.”The petition received more than 25,000 signatures within a week. Zelenskyy subsequently said parliament would consider legislation to legalise pornography.The bill co-authored by Zhelezniak passed its first reading in Ukraine's parliament in July and is due to face a second reading.War puts pressure on Ukraine's financesThe proposed legislation comes as Ukraine continues to face heavy financial demands from its prolonged war with Russia. Kyiv is seeking additional resources to fund defence, military equipment and other wartime needs.Ukraine has also increasingly relied on domestically produced drones and other unmanned systems as it seeks to reduce dependence on foreign weapons supplies and maintain its ability to strike Russian military and infrastructure targets.Among the systems developed or used by Ukraine are long-range strike drones, missile-drone hybrids, guided rocket systems, naval drones and ground robots. Millions of smaller FPV drones have also become a key part of battlefield operations.The growing domestic weapons industry allows Ukraine to continue developing and producing military systems despite uncertainty over foreign aid. It also gives Kyiv greater flexibility as it seeks to sustain the war effort. However, the systems face challenges including Russian electronic warfare, air defences and attacks on Ukrainian production facilities.The war continues to place significant pressure on Ukraine's economy and public finances, increasing the importance of finding additional sources of revenue.

articles.title: ‘Reset to zero’: Russia warns US missile deployment in Norway threatens nuclear talks
articles.summary: Europe News: Russia has criticised the United States for deploying a new missile system in Norway, warning that the move could further damage already strained effo.
articles.body: Russia has criticised the United States for deploying a new missile system in Norway, warning that the move could further damage already strained efforts by Moscow and Washington to discuss nuclear and strategic stability.The Russian Foreign Ministry said the system installed in Norway uses Mk-41 launchers capable of firing different types of missiles, including Tomahawk cruise missiles. Moscow said the deployment was particularly concerning because missiles launched from the system could reach a large part of European Russia, including the Russian capital.Moscow warns of consequencesIn a statement, the foreign ministry said the deployment of US ground-based intermediate-range missiles in Europe undermined the possibility of meaningful discussions with Washington on strategic issues."Steps such as the ​deployment in ​Europe of US ground-based intermediate range ⁠missiles that pose a threat to the ​Russian Federation 'reset to zero' - to put it ​mildly - the conditions for constructive dialogue with the US on strategic issues," the ministry said.Russia also issued a direct warning over the locations of the missile systems.It said Moscow would pay "particular attention" to the sites where US missile systems are deployed, as well as their command-and-control centres. According to the ministry, these locations would be considered targets if a military conflict were to break out.US deployment reported in AugustUS media reports said Washington had delivered the new missile launch system to Norway in August.The Mk-41 launcher is a versatile system that can be configured to fire different missiles. Russia's concern centres on the possibility that such systems could be used to launch weapons capable of striking deep into Russian territory.Russia dismisses wider nuclear talksThe Russian foreign ministry also criticised the state of strategic stability discussions between Moscow and Washington.It said talks on strategic stability had been curtailed under the previous US administration. Moscow also rejected as "unrealistic" plans by the current administration to pursue broader negotiations on strategic issues that would include China.The latest dispute comes as Russia and the US remain at odds over missile deployments and the future of nuclear arms control, with Moscow warning that the new system in Norway could make an already difficult dialogue even harder.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: “Supervision till 16 isn’t control, it’s care”: Shilpa Shetty on the one internet rule parents should not ignore while raising children
articles.summary: For parents, giving a child a phone is rarely just about giving them a device. It also means giving them access to videos, games, social media, strang.
articles.body: For parents, giving a child a phone is rarely just about giving them a device. It also means giving them access to videos, games, social media, strangers, misinformation and content they may not yet know how to process. Actor Shilpa Shetty spoke about this balance on the occasion of Safer Internet Day in February this year, asking parents to look beyond simply restricting screen time.In a video shared on Instagram, she said she was speaking “not as a public figure, but as a concerned mother” and urged parents to have more open conversations about what children do online. “The Internet is a powerful teacher, a playground for creativity,” Shilpa said. “So with the pros comes the cons, and we must be aware of them.”“It can also expose young minds to things that they're not ready for. And as parents, our role isn't to just simply ban technology. It's to balance the access and exposure to it.” That balance, however, can be difficult.Parents want to protect their children, but children increasingly use the internet for schoolwork, entertainment, friendships and discovering the world around them. Taking the phone away may stop one problem temporarily, but it does not teach a child what to do when something disturbing appears on the screen.Shilpa's advice starts with knowing what a child is consuming. “Know what your child is watching, scrolling, consuming,” she said. She also stressed the importance of talking instead of relying entirely on restrictions. “Curiosity grows in silence, not in conversation,” she said in the video.“Supervision till 16, I believe, isn’t control. It’s care”The most striking part of Shilpa's message was her view on parental supervision. “Please use parental controls. But more importantly, build trust,” she said. “Supervision till 16, I believe, isn’t control. It’s care.” The statement raises an important question for parents: what should supervision actually look like?There is a difference between knowing what platforms a child uses and secretly reading every private conversation. There is also a difference between setting age-appropriate restrictions and monitoring a child so closely that they stop feeling trusted. Good digital supervision should ideally change as the child grows.A 10-year-old may need parents to decide which apps are appropriate. A 13-year-old may need help understanding privacy, online friendships and inappropriate content. A 15-year-old may need more independence, but still needs to know that a parent is available when something goes wrong. The aim should be to gradually transfer responsibility to the child rather than suddenly handing over complete freedom.Don't wait for the first online crisis to have the conversationOne practical mistake parents can make is talking about internet safety only after something happens. A child sees an inappropriate video. Someone sends a disturbing message. A stranger asks for a photograph. A friend shares a private image. Only then does the parent sit down for a serious conversation. By that point, the child may already be frightened about telling them.Instead, parents can have small, ordinary conversations long before there is a problem. Ask what they watched today. Which creator do they like? What games are they playing? What do their friends discuss online?Teach children what to do when something goes wrongInternet safety is not just about preventing children from seeing harmful content. It is also about preparing them for the moment they inevitably encounter something they were not expecting. Parents can teach a simple three-step response: Stop. Don't respond. Tell an adult. If someone online makes a child uncomfortable, asks for personal information, sends inappropriate material or pressures them to keep a conversation secret, the child should know they can leave the conversation and tell a trusted adult. Most importantly, parents should make one thing clear that telling the truth will not automatically result in the phone being taken away.Parental controls are useful, but they cannot replace parentingShilpa also urged parents to use parental controls. These tools can help parents manage age restrictions, purchases, screen time and access to certain content. But a parental-control setting cannot teach a child why a stranger asking for their school name is a red flag. It cannot explain why a viral video may be edited or false. And it cannot help a teenager deal with cyberbullying.That is why technology controls work best when paired with conversations. Parents can even involve older children in setting the rules. Instead of simply announcing, “You get one hour of screen time,” discuss when the phone can be used, which apps are allowed and what happens if a rule is broken. When children understand the reason behind a rule, they are more likely to follow it.One rule parents should avoidTrust does not mean giving children unlimited privacy at every age. But constant surveillance can also backfire. If a teenager knows that every message, search and photograph may be checked without warning, they may become better at hiding things rather than better at making safe choices. A healthier approach is to establish expectations in advance. Parents can tell children: “Your privacy matters, but your safety matters more. If I become worried about something serious, I may need to step in. I will tell you rather than secretly monitoring you.”That keeps the door open for intervention while respecting the child's growing independence.Teach children one important internet ruleShilpa said, “Teach them that not everything online is real, kind, or even safe.” That lesson covers much more than fake news. Children need to understand that people may present an edited version of their lives online. Influencers may be paid to promote products. Videos can be manipulated. Strangers may pretend to be someone else. A large number of followers does not make a person trustworthy. For teenagers especially, this can become a regular family conversation rather than a one-time lecture.Shilpa ended her message by saying she does not have all the answers but wants to “start a real conversation”. She also urged parents to stop “parenting in isolation” and work towards raising “digitally aware and not digitally addicted children”. The goal cannot realistically be to keep children away from the internet. They will eventually use it for education, work, friendships and everyday life. The more useful goal is to raise a child who knows when to put the phone down, when to question what they see, when to block someone, when to ask for help and when an online interaction has crossed a line.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.body: Barack Obama's words are a genuinely honest reminder that meaningful achievement rarely happens quickly, and almost never without a real setback along the way. "Making your mark on the world is hard," he said. "If it were easy, everybody would do it. But it's not. It takes patience, it takes commitment and it comes with plenty of failure along the way." This line comes from a college commencement address he delivered in 2012, reported by NPR that same year in a segment covering that season's graduation speeches. Obama continued the thought considerably further, saying, "The real test is not whether you avoid this failure, because you won't. It's whether you let it harden or shame you into inaction, or whether you learn from it, whether you choose to persevere." Making a lasting contribution to anything worthwhile, whether through a career or a genuinely creative pursuit, usually demands considerably more than raw talent alone.Quote of the day by Barack Obama"Making your mark on the world is hard. If it were easy, everybody would do it. But it's not. It takes patience, it takes commitment and it comes with plenty of failure along the way"What is the meaning of Barack Obama's quoteObama is genuinely saying that making a meaningful impact is difficult precisely because it requires qualities not everyone is actually willing to develop. If success were genuinely easy, almost everyone would achieve exactly the same level of recognition, and the fact that it is difficult means people genuinely have to stay committed even when results are not immediate. His reference to failure is particularly important here. A setback is presented not as evidence that someone should automatically quit, but as a genuinely expected part of pursuing anything actually worthwhile.Why patience genuinely matters when pursuing successMany genuine goals take considerably longer than people initially expect. Whether someone is building a career or learning an entirely new skill, real progress can be genuinely uneven, and there may be long stretches where the effort produces very little visible result. Patience is what allows people to genuinely keep working through those stretches, rather than abandoning a real goal simply because success has not arrived quickly enough.Why commitment matters more than temporary motivationMotivation genuinely changes from one day to the next. There will be days when working toward a goal feels genuinely exciting, and others when it feels considerably more exhausting or frustrating. Commitment provides something genuinely more stable than either mood. It means continuing to actually take action even when enthusiasm is temporarily missing, and that consistency can be exactly what separates a short-lived attempt from a genuinely long-term pursuit.Why failure is genuinely part of the journeyObama's quote never presents failure as an unusual event. Instead, he describes it as something that genuinely comes "along the way," and that distinction genuinely matters. A failed attempt does not necessarily mean the overall goal has actually failed. It can reveal what genuinely needs to change, or which approach was unlikely to work in the first place. Failure becomes genuinely useful specifically when people are willing to actually examine it, rather than simply fearing it outright, which is really the whole point of his fuller continuation about not letting failure "harden or shame you into inaction."Why making a real difference genuinely takes timeSome of the most genuinely meaningful accomplishments are built gradually. A person may spend real years developing expertise before receiving any recognition at all, and a creative project may genuinely require countless attempts before it actually reaches its potential. The final result can genuinely make the whole process look effortless from the outside, when behind it usually sit real years of work that stayed largely invisible to everyone else watching.The genuine difference between success and instant resultsModern culture can genuinely make success appear immediate. People often see only the finished product rather than the actual years of preparation sitting behind it. Obama's quote genuinely challenges that perception by putting the real emphasis back on the process itself. Patience and commitment matter because meaningful progress is very often genuinely cumulative, and small improvement repeated over a genuinely long period can eventually produce a result that would have been completely impossible through occasional bursts of effort alone.How to genuinely handle a setback without simply giving upA real setback can be genuinely discouraging, particularly once someone has invested considerable time into something. One genuinely useful approach is to separate the actual goal from the method used to reach it. If one approach genuinely fails, it does not automatically mean the goal itself was impossible. Sometimes the real strategy simply needs to change, and this mindset genuinely lets failure become useful information rather than some kind of final verdict on your ability.What this quote genuinely teaches about perseveranceGenuine perseverance was never simply about continuing to do exactly the same thing regardless of the actual results. Effective perseverance genuinely involves learning and adapting along the way. A person can genuinely remain committed to a goal while still changing their actual methods, seeking real advice, or trying a considerably different approach entirely. That combination of persistence and real flexibility is what genuinely makes a long-term goal considerably more achievable.Other popular quotes by Barack Obama"Change will not come if we wait for some other person, or if we wait for some other time. We are the ones we've been waiting for. We are the change that we seek.""Focusing your life solely on making a buck shows a poverty of ambition. It asks too little of yourself.""You can't let your failures define you. You have to let your failures teach you.""If you're walking down the right path and you're willing to keep walking, eventually you'll make progress."How to apply Barack Obama's lessonBe genuinely patient, giving a meaningful goal enough real time to actually develop properly. Stay genuinely committed, continuing to work even while motivation naturally fluctuates from one day to the next. Expect real setbacks, since genuine difficulty never automatically means actual failure. Learn honestly from a genuine mistake, treating an unsuccessful attempt as useful information rather than a final verdict, and adapt your actual approach once the evidence genuinely suggests something is not working. Focus on real progress rather than instant results, since small improvement genuinely accumulates over time, and avoid comparing your own timeline with someone else's, since their genuinely visible achievement may well hide years of invisible work behind it.Why Barack Obama's quote remains relevantThe genuine pressure to achieve quickly can make an entirely ordinary setback feel like a major failure. Obama's words offer a considerably more realistic perspective instead, that genuinely important achievement is difficult, takes real time, and rarely happens without some actual failure along the way. That does not mean every genuinely difficult goal should be pursued indefinitely regardless of the evidence. It means real difficulty and setback should never automatically be interpreted as reasons to simply quit. Sometimes the actual process of trying, failing, learning and trying again is genuinely exactly how meaningful progress happens. Making your mark was never really about avoiding failure altogether. It requires having enough real patience and genuine commitment to actually learn from failure and keep moving forward regardless.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: US issues security warning, restricts government travel to Mexican border city Nogales
articles.summary: US News: The US Consulate General has restricted travel for government employees in Nogales, Mexico, due to an unspecified security threat, urging citizens to exercise caution and monitor local news.
articles.body: Travel and official activity for US government employees in Nogales, Mexico, have been restricted following an unspecified security threat reported in the border city.The US Embassy and Consulates in Mexico issued the alert on Saturday. The US Consulate General in Nogales said in a statement: “Due to threat information, U.S. government activities in, and travel to, Nogales have been restricted to essential movement during daylight hours only.”“We are alerting U.S. citizens of this threat and change in posture,” the statement added.The consulate did not identify the threat or provide details about the information behind the warning.Mexican authorities said they had contacted US consular officials after the alert was issued. Sonora’s State Security Board said it had not received information pointing to a specific threat or an immediate danger to the public.The state security agency said preventive operations would continue in Nogales.The warning comes with Sonora already classified by the US State Department as a Level 3 destination, meaning Americans are advised to “Reconsider Travel.”US citizens in Nogales have been urged to remain alert, monitor local news and follow instructions from Mexican authorities. The guidance also advises people to seek shelter if an incident occurs and inform family or friends of their safety.US Rep. Andy Biggs, a Republican from Arizona, urged Americans in and around Nogales to follow the government’s safety guidance.“We are praying for the safety of US citizens and personnel who may be in harm’s way,” Biggs said in a post on X.The nature of the threat that led to the latest restrictions has not been disclosed.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Akhilesh's 'chavanni' jab: Can Jayant Chaudhary be BJP’s trump card in western UP?
articles.summary: India News: Akhilesh Yadav may have intended \"chavanni\" as a put-down, but in Uttar Pradesh politics, old coins have a habit of changing hands and sometimes gaini.
articles.body: Akhilesh Yadav may have intended "chavanni" as a put-down, but in Uttar Pradesh politics, old coins have a habit of changing hands and sometimes gaining value in the process. Three years after Jayant Chaudhary insisted he was no "chavanni" to be flipped, the coin metaphor has made a comeback, this time from his former ally, just as the RLD chief prepares for another electoral test in western UP.The row began when Akhilesh, without naming Jayant, said: "Humne chavanni ka rupya bana diya tha, tab bhi humein chhod kar chale gaye wo" — we turned a 25-paise coin into a rupee, yet they left us. The remark was widely seen as a jibe at the RLD chief, who had once used the same "chavanni" metaphor while rejecting speculation that he could switch sides.Jayant's response was swift. "Siyasat ki ladai mein kuch saste shabd bolne hi the, to mera naam lekar bol dete, koi baat nahi thi," he said. He accused Akhilesh of targeting the Jat community and added: "Main is ahankar ko dekh chuka hoon kareeb se aur maanta hoon aisa aacharan sirf patan laata hai" — I have seen this arrogance from close quarters and believe such conduct only leads to downfall.Meanwhile, Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath also jumped in and hit back at Akhilesh, saying the language used against political opponents was making a "mockery of democracy" while describing the remark as an insult to Jayant, the legacy of Chaudhary Charan Singh and the farming community.The exchange may look like little more than pre-election sparring. But it points to a bigger question: why is Jayant Chaudhary important enough for both sides to keep talking about him?Jayant is no longer merely a smaller ally being wooed by rival camps. He is a Union minister, heads a party that won both Lok Sabha seats it contested in 2024 and carries the Chaudhary family name into a region where Jats and farmers remain central to the political arithmetic.So, ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly election, the real question is less about whether Akhilesh turned a "chavanni" into a rupee and more about how much political currency that rupee can buy in western UP.The 'coin' that changed handsIn the 2024 Lok Sabha election, Jayant's RLD posted a 100% strike rate, winning both seats it contested while in alliance with the BJP.But the picture was very different in the assembly elections.In 2017, the party was reduced to a marginal force in Uttar Pradesh, winning just one seat with around 1.5% of the vote share.However, in 2022, as it entered an alliance with the Samajwadi Party, the RLD contested 33 seats and won eight, with its vote share rising to nearly 3%.But the revival was not entirely an SP creation.Jayant had already begun rebuilding his political base, and the 2020-21 farmers' protests gave him an opportunity to re-establish himself as one of western UP's prominent political faces. Through kisan panchayats and sustained attacks on the NDA government over the farm laws and sugarcane dues, he reconnected with sections of a Jat electorate that had moved towards the BJP after the communal polarisation following the 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots.The SP-RLD alliance therefore worked both ways. The SP provided the RLD electoral space and organisational support, while Jayant offered the SP access to a Jat political network in a region where the BJP had built a formidable base.The numbers underline both the limits and value of that alliance. The RLD won eight of the 33 seats it contested in 2022, but the BJP won all 25 seats that the RLD lost.The RLD had regained relevance in pockets of western UP, but it was nowhere close to being a statewide challenger.Akhilesh may therefore have a point when he says the SP helped turn the RLD's "chavanni" into a rupee. But that is only half the transaction.Jayant brought the SP something that could not be created simply through seat-sharing - a political bridge to sections of the Jat electorate and the symbolic capital of the Chaudhary family.How BJP 'won' RLD chief's heartIn February 2024, the BJP and RLD announced their alliance, with the BJP offering the smaller party two Lok Sabha seats and a Rajya Sabha berth.The announcement came shortly after the Centre conferred the Bharat Ratna on former prime minister Chaudhary Charan Singh, a move Jayant publicly welcomed.He immediately posted on X: "Dil jeet liya" - won the heart.When asked whether the post meant the RLD would join the BJP, Jayant replied: "Koi kasar rehti hai? Aaj main kis muh se inkaar karoon aapke sawalon ko?" - Is there anything left? How can I deny your questions today?The RLD then contested Baghpat and Bijnor in the 2024 Lok Sabha election and won both.For the BJP, however, the bigger prize was a political intermediary who could speak to sections of the Jat electorate on behalf of the NDA while carrying the Chaudhary name.The BJP's relationship with Jayant Chaudhary's party and family had also undergone a dramatic reversal.In 2014, the BJP swept western Uttar Pradesh, defeating then-RLD chief Ajit Singh in Baghpat and his son Jayant in Mathura. Five years later, the father-son duo suffered another setback, losing in Muzaffarnagar and Baghpat respectively.But the saffron party subsequently lost some ground among Jats amid the farmers' protests and the long-running demand for reservation.Jayant's entry into the NDA therefore gave the BJP a recognised Jat face at a time when the opposition was trying to rebuild a broader farmer-minority coalition in the region.Why Jats matter in western UPThere is no recent official caste census providing a definitive figure for the Jat population in Uttar Pradesh. Estimates commonly put Jats at around 2% of the state's population, but their concentration in western UP gives them much greater political weight in the region. Estimates have put their share at roughly 17-18% in the area often described as "Jatland".They heavily sway the electoral outcomes of roughly 40 to 45 assembly seats and about 10 to 12 Lok Sabha (parliamentary) seats in western UP.There is also a historical reason the Jat vote matters.Before the 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots, the politics of Chaudhary Charan Singh and later Ajit Singh rested in part on a cross-community farmer coalition involving Jats and Muslims. The riots fractured that relationship and pushed many Jats towards the BJP.The farmers' movement briefly reopened the possibility of a Jat-Muslim political convergence that the SP-RLD alliance tried to convert into votes in 2022.Jayant's subsequent move to the NDA, however, made that opposition combination considerably harder to sustain.For the BJP, therefore, Jayant may be useful not simply because he can attract Jats, but because his presence can also complicate the social coalition Akhilesh is trying to build.The Jayant question in Akhilesh's PDA strategyThat brings the RLD directly into Akhilesh's larger PDA strategy — Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak — which seeks to bring backward classes, Dalits and minorities together while reducing the SP's dependence on its traditional Yadav base.The 2024 Lok Sabha election demonstrated the potential of that strategy, with the SP emerging as the largest party in Uttar Pradesh.For the BJP, the challenge ahead of 2027 will be to prevent that coalition from consolidating, particularly in regions where the party faces a more competitive opposition.Jayant is one piece of that counter-strategy.The RLD, meanwhile, appears keen to expand beyond its traditional Jat base. Its outreach has included Gurjars and other communities, while party leaders have spoken of a broader AJGR formula - Ahir, Jat, Gurjar and Rajput - along with efforts to reach Dalits and Muslims.Why September 3 rally mattersThat is why the RLD's September 3 'Swabhiman Rally' in Saharanpur mattered beyond its immediate spat with Akhilesh.The rally was an attempt to demonstrate that Jayant can still mobilise on his own political terms rather than functioning merely as a BJP ally.And Jayant used the "chavanni" controversy to turn criticism into an argument for relevance."Jo abhi gaaliyan de rahe hain, abhi to sun lo... sahi samay par nipat lenge," he said — those abusing us should listen for now; they will be dealt with at the appropriate time. He then added that the fact that opposition leaders kept mentioning the RLD showed that the party was working in the "right place and in the right direction."(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();But the more significant part of his pitch was directed at farmers, the community most closely associated with the Chaudhary family's political legacy.Calling on farmers to identify their "true supporters" and choose a strong political advocate, Jayant said: "Farmers are in a majority and governments are made and unmade on their strength, but the hard reality is that the farmers’ lobby is weak in political corridors. Therefore, farmers need to choose a strong advocate for their cause."This could be seen as more than a regular rallying cry. It was a reminder of what Jayant believes his political value rests on: being the voice of a region and a community larger than the RLD's current electoral footprint.But how much is Jayant worth?The 2027 seat-sharing exercise could be the clearest measure yet of Jayant's political "worth".A meaningful allocation of seats would suggest that the BJP believes the RLD's organisation can add value across western UP. A sharply limited share, on the other hand, would indicate that the BJP sees little reason to give Jayant enough room to build an independent base.Jayant also has something to prove.The RLD's two Lok Sabha victories in 2024 demonstrated that the party could convert its alliance with the BJP into electoral success. The next test is whether it can build enough support beyond those two constituencies to negotiate from a position of strength.Now, ahead of the 2027 elections, the question is whether Jayant can convert that symbolic capital into enough independent political influence to remain indispensable to the BJP.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: An Australian woman bought cleared sugarcane land and planted trees; 10 years later, 119,000 trees transformed it into a rainforest home to flying-foxes
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Annie Schoenberger bought cleared land near Wonga Beach in Queensland, Australia, with a simple but ambitious goal of bringing rainforest back to a pr.
articles.body: Annie Schoenberger bought cleared land near Wonga Beach in Queensland, Australia, with a simple but ambitious goal of bringing rainforest back to a property once used for sugarcane. What followed was a decade-long restoration effort at her NightWings Rainforest Centre, where native trees were planted with the help of Rainforest Rescue, volunteers and supporters. More than 119,000 trees have now been planted across 18 hectares, gradually replacing the cleared agricultural landscape with young rainforest habitat. The project has also attracted native wildlife and helped restore wetland areas and improve water quality. In May 2026, the restoration reached another major milestone when the Queensland Government recognised the 18-hectare area as being of high nature conservation value, giving the recovering vegetation Category A protection under Queensland's vegetation management framework.From cleared sugarcane land to a young rainforestSchoenberger purchased the property in 2014 after much of the land had been cleared for sugarcane farming. She wanted to restore the landscape to lowland Daintree rainforest and create habitat for native wildlife. Restoration work began in 2015, followed by the first community tree-planting event in 2016. Rainforest Rescue became a major partner in the effort, helping organise planting events, supply rainforest seedlings and bring volunteers together to restore the former agricultural land.The original restoration target was around 15 hectares, but the area eventually expanded to 18 hectares. Instead of establishing a conventional plantation, the project focused on planting a diverse selection of native rainforest species that could gradually recreate the structure and ecological functions of the original forest.More than 119,000 trees planted over a decadeThe transformation was built through repeated planting efforts rather than a single large-scale operation. Over 10 years, volunteers, conservation workers and supporters returned to NightWings to put thousands of native seedlings into the ground.Rainforest Rescue's latest 2026 update says more than 119,000 trees had been planted at NightWings, with the final planting completed in 2025. The organisation says the decade-long effort involved hundreds of people who helped Schoenberger turn the cleared property into a growing rainforest landscape.The planting has also focused on species diversity. At a 2023 community planting day, more than 140 people planted 3,300 trees representing about 90 rainforest species. Such diversity is important because rainforest restoration is intended to recreate a functioning ecosystem rather than simply increase the number of trees.Wildlife began using the recovering habitatAs vegetation grew, the restored property began providing habitat and food resources for wildlife. NightWings is particularly connected to the spectacled flying-fox, a species Schoenberger has cared for through her wildlife rehabilitation work.Southern cassowaries have also been recorded at the property. A juvenile cassowary was photographed at NightWings in 2018, with Rainforest Rescue describing the sighting as particularly significant because it was the first recorded sighting south of the Daintree River in more than four decades. Later observations have continued to demonstrate that native wildlife is using the recovering landscape.Other fauna recorded around the property include various birds, mammals, reptiles, frogs and bats. Surveys have recorded more than 75 fauna species, including several species listed as endangered, vulnerable or near threatened.The wildlife records do not mean that every species returned solely because of the restoration, but they provide evidence that the recovering vegetation is being used as habitat.The restoration helped rebuild wetland habitatTree planting was only one part of the restoration. Wetland habitat at NightWings has also been restored, adding another type of ecosystem to the property.Rainforest Rescue has reported improvements in water quality associated with the restoration, including reduced sediment and turbidity entering nearby waterways. Re-establishing vegetation can help stabilise soil, slow runoff and create conditions that support healthier waterways.The location is also important because the property sits within the Wet Tropics region of Queensland, an area known for its exceptional rainforest biodiversity and its ecological connection to surrounding coastal environments.A former farm became a wildlife corridorThe restoration was intended to do more than improve a single property. Re-establishing rainforest on cleared land can help reconnect fragmented habitat, giving wildlife additional areas through which to move, feed and shelter.NightWings forms part of the broader effort to restore lowland rainforest in the Daintree region, where agricultural and other development have historically removed or fragmented sections of native vegetation.For Schoenberger, the project also had a personal connection. Her work caring for flying-foxes helped shape her desire to create a landscape where native fruiting trees could provide food and habitat for wildlife rather than leaving the animals dependent entirely on fragmented natural areas.The 18 hectares gained conservation protectionThe biggest development came in May 2026, when the Queensland Government formally recognised the restored NightWings vegetation as an area of high nature conservation value under the Vegetation Management Act 1999.The 18 hectares are now mapped as Category A vegetation on Queensland's regulated vegetation management map. This gives the restored vegetation a higher level of protection against clearing and formally recognises the conservation importance of the recovering forest.The designation is particularly notable because the land was once used for agriculture. A landscape that had been cleared for sugarcane is now recognised by the state for its conservation value after a decade of restoration.A decade turned a cleared landscape into a restoration successNightWings shows how long-term restoration can gradually change land that had been cleared for agriculture. Schoenberger bought the former sugarcane property, began restoring it with conservation partners and continued the effort for a decade as volunteers planted tens of thousands of native trees.By the completion of planting in 2025, Rainforest Rescue reported more than 119,000 trees planted across the restoration area. In 2026, the 18 hectares of restored vegetation gained recognition as an area of high nature conservation value and Category A protection.The forest is still young and its ecological development will continue for decades, but the transformation is already substantial. What began as cleared sugarcane land is now a growing rainforest landscape providing habitat for native wildlife and carrying formal recognition for its conservation value.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: UN agency accused of Hamas ties sees another European nation cut funding
articles.summary: Finland will discontinue UNRWA funding by end of 2026, following the Trump administration and Sweden in cutting ties with the Hamas-linked U.N. agency.
articles.body: Another European nation has stopped funding the U.N. agency that aids the Palestinians. Finland has followed the U.S. and Sweden in halting donations to the terror-tainted agency. The United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA), is presently being investigated for ties to the terrorist rulers of Gaza. Recently, organizations including the USAID Office of Inspector General (OIG) and NGO UN Watch have uncovered further evidence of what they allege is Hamas infiltration of UNRWA and its members’ participation in the Oct. 7, 2023 terror attacks in southern Israel. Finland announced it would discontinue funding to the organization at the end of 2026. Finland’s Ministry for Foreign Affairs confirmed to Fox News Digital that the agreement with UNRWA would conclude at the end of 2026 but that "As of yet, no decision has been made on what are the international partners through which Finland’s support will be channeled next year to meet the acute needs in the region." Finnish officials did not respond to Fox News Digital’s questions about what prompted the change to the country’s funding for UNRWA. US URGES DONORS TO ABANDON UNRWA FUNDING AS UN DEFENDS AGENCY'S MISSION While other nations still continue to fund UNRWA, President Donald Trump fully banned funding to the organization in February 2025, and Sweden ended funding to UNRWA in December 2024. Sweden redirected aid to other U.N. bodies for its Gaza response. The future of aid provision in Gaza matters for the Trump administration-backed Board of Peace as it seeks to shape a conflict-free future for the region. An official affiliated with the Board of Peace reconstruction effort told Fox News Digital that "the international community’s concern about UNRWA in Gaza continues to rise and is supported by damning evidence. The Board of Peace has been clear: New Gaza will be both demilitarized and deradicalized, and we will only be working with trusted, credible delivery partners to achieve our goals. We anticipate responsibly replacing UNRWA with vetted partners who will deliver for the people of Gaza." WATCHDOG DEMANDS APOLOGY AFTER UN MEMORIAL ERRONEOUSLY HONORS HAMAS TERRORIST The USAID OIG is investigating about 1,500 members of UNRWA for terror participation, and has referred 108 UNRWA staff to the State Department to suggest they be suspended or excluded from further work with organizations in receipt of U.S. funds. A senior U.S. official briefed on USAID OIG’s ongoing investigation told Fox News Digital that the USAID OIG’s "independent findings are prompting several other countries to reassess the stale and conventional thinking that UNRWA is the best and only option to provide aid to civilians in Gaza." The official said that the USAID OIG’s "findings also will prevent Hamas and October 7 affiliated staff from circulating across future, more responsible, aid organizations operating in Gaza." WORLD'S HUMANITARIAN SYSTEM BUCKLING, 'NO LONGER FIT FOR PURPOSE,' US-BASED RESEARCHERS SAY UN Watch’s Terror Network report claims that about 12% of UNRWA staff in Gaza are members of terror organizations, based on "cross-checking UNRWA employee rosters with Hamas records seized by the [Israel Defense Forces.]" Executive director of UN Watch Hillel Neuer told Fox News Digital that "Finland’s principled decision to defund terror-infested UNRWA will not deprive Palestinians of aid, as it will be redirected through genuine humanitarian agencies such as the World Food Programme that are not systemically infiltrated by Hamas." He said that "other democracies should follow" the examples of Finland, Sweden, and the U.S. "Contrary to what UNRWA supporters claim, the agency is not ‘indispensable’ — assistance can and must be delivered through responsible alternatives." Stéphane Dujarric, spokesperson for U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres, told Fox News Digital that "UNRWA has taken note of the announcement, and they are grateful to Finland for the disbursement of the 2023–2026 funds under the multi-year agreement. UNRWA looks forward to continuing our discussions with the government." He explained that "the Secretary-General continues to encourage member states to support UNRWA's vital work." Finland's four-year funding was around $23.23 million to UNRWA and will now end after this year. UNRWA did not respond to Fox News Digital questions about Finland’s decision. Neuer said "defunding UNRWA is a prerequisite for deradicalization, the first step in the Gaza peace plan. Far from harming the prospects for peace, dismantling UNRWA is essential to achieving it. For decades, the agency has perpetuated the conflict by teaching generations of Palestinians that their future lies not in building their own society, but in a so-called ‘right of return’ that would eliminate Israel." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP He concluded by noting that USAID OIG and UN Watch’s exposes on UNRWA prove that "the agency is unreformable. Nations that genuinely want peace should stop financing this machinery of hate, and invest instead in humanitarian relief, deradicalization and Palestinian self-reliance."

articles.title: Cops injured, vehicles damaged as anti‑migrant protest turns violent in UK; second protest in two days
articles.summary: UK News: An anti-migrant demonstration in Portsmouth escalated into violence resulting in injuries to police officers and damage to emergency service vehicles. The protest followed the arrival of 140 migrants by boat, raising concerns about safety and suitability of the disembarkation site.
articles.body: Several police officers were injured and vehicles belonging to police, Coastguard and Border Force were damaged after an anti-migrant protest in Portsmouth turned violent following the arrival of about 140 migrants by boat.Hundreds of people gathered in the English coastal city on Sunday after two RNLI boats brought migrants ashore. Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary said officers and other emergency service personnel were attacked during the disorder, Sky News reported.“A small number of officers were treated at the scene, but no one from any agency or the public was seriously injured,” the force said.The demonstration was brought to an end at about 4am on Monday, according to the outlet.The migrants had been travelling in a dinghy that was intercepted in the English Channel on Sunday. The boat had departed from the Jobourg area of Normandy in northern France before being met by two RNLI vessels, which took those on board to Portsmouth.The journey was believed to be among the longest undertaken by a small boat carrying migrants, with arrivals this far west on the English coast relatively uncommon.Portsmouth council leader Steve Pitt criticised the decision to use the location for the disembarkation, saying the Home Office had "serious questions to answer" over what he described as an unsuitable site that “put people at risk”.The protest came a day after a separate demonstration in Dover, where about 200 masked protesters blocked access roads to the port for several hours while chanting "Stop the boats"Kent Police said the disruption had caused significant traffic problems but confirmed that wearing a face covering was not, by itself, a criminal offence.Assistant Chief Constable Nigel Brookes said there was "no need" for people to cover their faces if they intended to protest peacefully.The Portsmouth disorder has prompted condemnation from minister Emma Reynolds, who described those involved as "thuggish".Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) has surged to first place in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt, winning 44% of the vote. But the anti-immigrant, pro-Russian party fell three seats short of an absolute majority, meaning it must either find a coalition partner or try to rule from a minority position.
articles.body: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) has surged to first place in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt, winning 44% of the vote. But the anti-immigrant, pro-Russian party fell three seats short of an absolute majority, meaning it must either find a coalition partner or try to rule from a minority position. Both options mean many of their manifesto ideas may never come to fruition, as mainstream parties in Germany have for years refused to work with the party, creating what has been dubbed a “firewall” against the far-right. One route might be a deal with the left-wing populist BSW party, which on Monday criticized the firewall and which shares some of the AfD’s criticism of Germany’s policies on immigration and Ukraine. AfD leaders in Saxony-Anhalt are also courting the more right-wing factions of the mainstream conservative Christian Democrats (CDU) – though Germany’s Chancellor Friedrich Merz has vehemently ruled out any cooperation. Discussions over potential alliances in the coming days will be critical for the future direction of the state, as Germany’s federal system gives its 16 states significant control over areas including education, culture, policing and public broadcasting. The AfD – a party German domestic intelligence has classified as “confirmed right wing extremist” – has made no secret of its desire to use power in Saxony-Anhalt as a blueprint for the rest of the nation. Its candidate for state premier, Ulrich Siegmund, told CNN on the campaign trail he hoped a victory for the party would spell the end of some of the “crazy” federal policies. But first, the party would have to contend with the budget shortfall in Saxony-Anhalt, and the challenges of transitioning from opposition to governing. As it sits on the cusp of power, here is a closer look at the party’s 258-page manifesto – a radical vision that showcases its aims for the state and beyond. ‘Remigration’ At the heart of the party’s manifesto is an overhaul of migration policy, including the immediate deportation of irregular migrants, the expansion of mass detention facilities and the return of non-ethnic-German citizens to their country of origin – a policy it refers to as “remigration.” The AfD argues that the region has “exhausted” its ability to accept refugees, “not only in terms of security policy, but also identity.” “People who are required to leave the country must be placed in deportation custody under our government,” Siegmund said in a recent interview. A section of the AfD’s manifesto calls for a “remigration offensive” against Ukrainian people, claiming they should be returned home because “large parts of Ukraine are considered safe.” However, Johannes Kieß, Deputy Director of the Else-Frenkel-Brunswik Institute (EFBI) for Democracy Research at Leipzig University, says migration policy is one of the most difficult to act on because states are limited by federal laws and regulations. “I would expect a great deal of legal uncertainty and chaos,” said Kieß. The AfD has also frequently called for Germany to end support for Ukraine and develop closer ties with Russia, putting it at odds with other major parties and the federal government, which has been the biggest backer of Ukraine since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022. Education: ‘More Bismarck, less Hitler’ Education is another key policy area for the AfD. Siegmund has pledged to overhaul Saxony-Anhalt’s school curriculum and “de-ideologize” school, including banning the Pride flag and promoting “traditional” German values. AfD politicians in Saxony-Anhalt want school lessons to focus on the periods of German history before World War I and World War II, and less on Germany’s Nazi past, in line with the party’s stated desire for Germans to move beyond guilt and focus on national pride. “More Bismarck, less Hitler,” is how Hans-Thomas Tillschneider, the party’s regional cultural spokesperson, summed it up in an interview with German media. “We want a completely new, a completely different education policy,” he said. “Political influence on children, as we experience it – political indoctrination – is not a job for schools.” The party’s manifesto also calls for segregated classes, with refugee children taught separately by other refugees, and teaching designed to convey the message that staying in Germany is temporary. Disabled children would also be taught separately under the plans. Culture: A crackdown on ‘anti-German art’ The AfD has promised what it calls a “new, patriotic cultural policy,” arguing that state institutions should play a more active role in promoting German national identity. As part of its state manifesto, the AfD has pledged to defund what it refers to as “anti-German” art. Asked to clarify what that means, Tillschneider said, “anti-German art is German art that doesn’t want to be German” and cited a performance he had seen where a classical German composer’s work was revised through a “feminist deconstructivism” lens. The AfD has said artists and institutions that want state funding would be required to sign a pledge that they will not hold Germany and its culture in contempt. The party’s manifesto states that the previous state government placed too much cultural significance on Bauhaus, Germany’s celebrated art school, as part of its “modern thinking” agenda. For the AfD, the movement lacks a sufficient German identity. Critics have noted the clear echoes in how the Nazis assaulted modern art. “The AfD is attacking the Bauhaus, using the very same words the Nazis used 100 years ago,” Culture Minister Wolfram Weimer told the Associated Press. “And that is why democrats, whether they lean conservative or left, are fighting back against it.” Kieß told CNN that Saxony-Anhalt would quickly become “poorer, both materially and culturally” from AfD policies. The end of the firewall? One of the biggest questions facing Germany following the AfD’s electoral success is the efficacy of the so-called “firewall” against the far right. It is now widely accepted that the policy could have contributed to the far-right’s rise by shielding it from the accountability that comes when parties hold office and face the reality of governing. The firewall also leads to rag-tag coalitions of mainstream parties, that have a difficult time finding policy agreements and getting things done in government. Even so, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s Christian Democratic Union and the other mainstream parties have pledged to keep the firewall in place. “If this result is not a mandate to govern, then what is?” Siegmund said at a news conference on Monday. “That is why it is now our goal to organize exactly such a stable majority in the coming days and weeks. … There are different ways this could happen: Either through the support, and indeed the full support, of a parliamentary group or individual members of parliament.” How things shake out in Saxony-Anhalt could have implications for two other regional elections in Germany this month. In the north-eastern state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, the AfD is leading with about 35%, according to the latest polling from Infratest dimap. Another strong showing for the AfD could also have wider-reaching implications for Germany’s next federal election, expected in 2029. Even though AfD only emerged in 2013, polls say that if national elections were held today, it would win most votes.

articles.title: Florida Gators revive iconic 'Gator Bait' chant the left deemed racist back in 2020, and fans ate it up
articles.summary: Florida Gators fans were thrilled as the iconic "Gator Bait" chant returned to the stands on Saturday after being shelved since the summer of 2020.
articles.body: The Florida Gators opened the first college football weekend of the season with a new coach, a new quarterback, and an offense that put up more points than it had in years. The most noticeable change, however, took place in the stands. The school revived the iconic, yet controversial, "Gator Bait" chant that had been shelved since America lost its mind during the summer of 2020. Like a lot of things, "Gator Bait" was deemed racist as the (very peaceful) social justice movement swept through the streets, and the school promptly shut it down. COLLEGE FOOTBALL'S FIRST FULL SATURDAY IS HERE AND IT'S A CELEBRATION OF AMERICA AT ITS BEST Now, six years later, it's back ... And fans were THRILLED: 'Gator Bait' was never racist Goodness, does that bring me back. I grew up going to Gators games during the Tebow era — the last good era, by the way — and that chant was electric. The band. The fans. The energy. It was the best. Of course, it was banned six years ago because folks suddenly decided it was racist. MIXED REVIEWS FOR 'GATOR BAIT' BAN Why? Well, the internet cooked up the idea that the chant originated from late-1800s and early-1900s imagery and stories that depicted Black children being used as bait to catch alligators. Yes, obviously that's just disgusting literature. Nobody is arguing that. Nobody did. But here's the thing ... then-UF President Kent Fuchs acknowledged at the time that the chant, which had been around for decades, had NOTHING to do with any of that. "While I know of no evidence of racism associated with our ‘Gator Bait’ cheer at UF sporting events, there is horrific historic racist imagery associated with the phrase," he wrote in a letter in June 2020. Translation: This isn't racist, but we're bending the knee to the mob because that's what everyone is doing right now. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS Fast-forward six years, and new Florida president Dr. Stuart Bell brought up the idea of reviving the iconic chant earlier this summer. "I know there’s a lot around the ‘Gator Bait’ (chant). It’s meaningful to the Gator family," Bell told 1010XL. "I hope we’re able to have some really great conversations around that." The chant, for those wondering, was coined the "Gator Bait" chant by Lawrence Wright way back in 1995. It was foolishly canceled in 2020, and smartly revived on Saturday. articles.title: Man arrested over fire that caused Heathrow rail disruption
articles.summary: Nearly 400 passengers had to be escorted from a train which lost power after overhead cables caught fire.
articles.body:
A man has been arrested on suspicion of arson following a grass fire near London Paddington station that caused major disruption to rail services.

Services affected from Saturday afternoon into Sunday morning included the Heathrow Express, the Elizabeth line and Great Western Railway trains out of Paddington towards Reading.

Almost 400 passengers had to be escorted from a train that lost power after overhead cables caught fire.

British Transport Police said the man has since been bailed.

articles.title: Israeli attacks on Gaza kill five Palestinians, including two children
articles.summary: Seven-year-old Wafaa Aqila and her father killed by Israeli strike while returning home with school supplies.
articles.body:
Israeli attacks on Gaza have killed five people, including two children, according to Palestinian officials, despite a so-called ceasefire in the war-ravaged territory.

Seven-year-old Wafaa Aqila and her father were killed by an Israeli strike on a vehicle they were travelling in after buying school supplies, just days before she was due to start the new school year, the Palestinian Ministry of Education said in a statement on Sunday.

Hours later, an Israeli artillery attack hit the Sakina School, which is serving as a shelter for displaced people in Deir el-Balah, killing Saadi Ghalia, a first-grade student.

The Palestinian Ministry of Education condemned the attacks, saying that while children around the world prepare for a new school year, in Gaza, children are subjected to “killing and annihilation”.

The Gaza Health Ministry reported on Monday that at least five Palestinians were killed and 30 others wounded in the past 24 hours, while two Palestinians died after succumbing to their wounds sustained in previous Israeli attacks.

At least 1,352 people have been killed and 4,511 others wounded since the “ceasefire” took effect in October, according to Health Ministry tallies. At least 73,658 Palestinians have been killed and 174,622 others wounded since Israel launched its genocidal war against Palestinians in Gaza in October 2023.

articles.title: Why are far-right masked men protesting at British ports?
articles.summary: Hundreds of balaclava-wearing protesters blocked roads and clashed with police in southern England overnight Sunday after a small boat carrying migrants landed on the coast, marking the second major anti-migration demonstration in the UK over the weekend.
articles.body: Hundreds of balaclava-wearing protesters blocked roads and clashed with police in southern England overnight Sunday after a small boat carrying migrants landed on the coast, marking the second major anti-migration demonstration in the UK over the weekend. Footage from the scene in the coastal city of Portsmouth showed the protesters, wearing mostly black, shouting “stop the boats” and “I’m England ‘til I die.” The group of far-right agitators had first attempted to stop lifeboats from bringing the migrants onto land before they staged a road protest where they sought to block buses from taking the asylum seekers to a processing facility. The standoff between police continued until early Monday morning. The protest appeared to be organized by a group called the Patriot Platform, led by Daniel Thomas, a former associate of the anti-Islamic, far-right political activist Tommy Robinson. The group calls itself a Christian “army of patriots,” who Thomas says are protesting for a “love for our children, country and most importantly the future that we are leaving for our children.” Also known as Danny Tommo, Thomas was jailed after pleading guilty for attempted kidnapping in 2016, British media reported. HOPE Not Hate, a British advocacy group that opposes far-right extremism, has been tracking Patriot Platform. HOPE Not Hate says the incident “shows the growing trend of anti-migrant vigilantism coming to a head in the public eye.” “Patriot Platform, and the smaller groups united by it, promote their ideology on the basis that they are providing a public service in the form of security in an ever-more dangerous Britain. In reality, Thomas has little hope of persuading others that Patriot Platform is a safety-first community group when its members march through the streets wearing balaclavas and have been exposed for their violent criminal records,” it said. The UK Home Office condemned “the intimidating and thuggish behaviour” in Portsmouth. “The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy, but it must never cross a line into disorder,” it said in a statement. A similar protest unfolded in Dover on Saturday, where video posted on social media from the busy port showed groups of men, also masked and dressed in black, linking arms across a main road and shouting “stop the boats.” The men blocked routes to the port, where ferries connect England to France. The protest caused a four-mile traffic jam on Saturday morning, according to the National Highways agency. No arrests were made in Portsmouth, according to the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary, which said that an investigation had been opened to “identify offenders responsible for any assaults to officers, criminal damage to vehicles, or other criminal offences.” No arrests were made in Dover, Kent Police said. Migration remains one of the most heated political issues in Britain, despite the number of migrants crossing the English Channel in small boats falling to its lowest level since 2020, according to the Home Office. The hard-right Reform UK party, whose popularity surged in England’s local elections in May, have particularly rallied around the issue of small boat crossings, with its leader, Nigel Farage, branding the asylum seekers “an invasion” in a speech on Friday. Farage told GB News Saturday that “nobody feels more strongly about stopping the boats than me,” but said he condemned the “disgusting” tactics taken this weekend. “Turning up in balaclavas is not the way to do it,” Farage said. Mike Tapp, a Labour party lawmaker who represents the constituency in Parliament, called the demonstrators “idiots coming to Dover to cause disruption.” “I bet if you asked any one of those ‘protesters’ they wouldn’t know small boat crossing are down by 40% and we are working hard to fix the mess,” he said in a Facebook post Saturday, adding: “Go home, enjoy your weekend/get a job.”
